questions.stem: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.solution: The SI unit of force is derived from Newton's second law, F = ma. Since the unit of mass is kg and the unit of acceleration is m/s², the unit of force is kg·m/s², which is equivalent to N (newton). The option 'kg m s^2' is incorrect because it implies the unit is kg·m·s², which is not the correct unit. The other options are either incorrect in their exponents or not standard units for force.

hi.stem: बल का एसआई मात्रक क्या है?
hi.solution: बल का एसआई मात्रक न्यूटन के द्वितीय नियम, F = ma से व्युत्पन्न होता है। द्रव्यमान का मात्रक किग्रा है और त्वरण का मात्रक मी/से² है, इसलिए बल का मात्रक किग्रा·मी/से² है, जो एन (न्यूटन) के बराबर है। विकल्प 'किग्रा मी स^2' गलत है क्योंकि इसका अर्थ है कि मात्रक किग्रा·मी·स² है, जो सही मात्रक नहीं है। अन्य विकल्प अपने घातांक में गलत हैं या बल के लिए मानक मात्रक नहीं हैं।

questions.stem: A sports car is moving with a constant acceleration of 2 m/s². What is the net force acting on the car if its mass is 1500 kg?
questions.solution: The net force acting on the car can be calculated using Newton's second law of motion, F = ma. Substituting the given values, F = 1500 kg × 2 m/s² = 3000 N. The option '3000 N' is correct because it accurately reflects the calculation. The other options are incorrect as they do not match the result of the calculation.

questions.stem: What happens to the acceleration of a system of two boxes if the force applied to the system is doubled?

questions.stem: When a box is pushed on a floor, what causes it to eventually stop moving after the pushing force is removed?
choices: The normal force exerted by the floor
questions.solution: The box stops moving because the force of friction, which acts in the opposite direction to the motion, gradually reduces the box's velocity until it comes to rest. The force of gravity and normal force are perpendicular to the motion and do not affect it. The net force is the result of all forces acting on the box and is not the direct cause of stopping.

questions.stem: A box is pushed on a horizontal surface. The force of friction is equal to the applied force. What happens to the box's velocity?
questions.solution: If the force of friction is equal to the applied force, the net force on the box is zero. This means the box will move with constant velocity. questions.solution: When the force applied by the person is removed, the only force acting on the box is the force of friction, which opposes the motion. questions.stem: A box is pushed on a horizontal surface and moves forward. After the push is removed, the box slows down and stops. If the same box is pushed on a smoother surface, what would happen?
choices: It would move with constant velocity
It would travel a longer distance before stopping
questions.solution: On a smoother surface, the force of friction is smaller. This means the box would take longer to stop and would travel a greater distance before coming to rest. It would not accelerate continuously because no net force is acting on it. The correct answer is that it would travel a longer distance before stopping.
